title: Sveskeblommer med Arrak (Dried Plums with Arrack)
description: Prepared with plums, sugar, and water.
steps: Place the dried pitted plums over heat with the specified amount of water.
Remove them as soon as they begin to boil and place in a sieve.
Once the water has drained well, place the plums in a crock.
Put the sugar in a pot together with the water from the plums and boil until it becomes a syrup that hangs in threads from the spoon.
Pour the boiling syrup over the plums and let them sit until the next day.
The next day, pour everything into the pot and remove the plums as soon as they boil.
Reduce the syrup before pouring it over the fruit.
The next day, pour enough good arrack over the plums to completely cover them and seal the crocks.

title: Sveskeblommer med Eddike (Prunes with Vinegar)
description: Prepared with vinegar, prunes, and sugar.
steps: Cover the prunes with boiling water and place on a sieve.
When sugar and vinegar are cooked to a thin syrup, add the prunes, but not more at once than can be ensured they do not break during cooking.
Cook only a couple of minutes, remove with a slotted spoon and spread on flat dishes until they have cooled and a glaze has formed over them; only then are they placed in the jar.
A little whole cinnamon is added to the liquid, which is cooked until smooth, which takes about 1 hour.
Treated in this way the prunes become excellent, and both pricking and drying are avoided.
If the liquid boils sufficiently long, it need not be reduced more often, and the prunes are sealed.
Should it happen that the liquid has become thin after some days, it is only the top that needs to be poured off and reduced.

title: Sveskeblommer uden Skind og Stene (Prunes without Skin and Stones)
description: Prepared with prunes, candied orange, and lemon.
steps: Place ripe prunes in boiling water until the skin comes off easily.
With a knife, cut a slit lengthwise along the prunes, through which the stones are removed; these can be crushed and the kernels cooked together with the prunes.
Cook sugar and water to syrup together with 50 gr succade, 50 gr candied orange peel, and the peel of 1 lemon, all cut into very fine, narrow strips.
When the syrup is cooked and skimmed, add the prunes, but not too many at once.
They must only just come to a boil and remain whole when removed with a slotted spoon and placed in the jar.
Reduce the syrup until smooth; then pour it over the prunes and seal.

After a week, check them, and should the liquid be too thin, pour off only the top, which is reduced and poured hot over the prunes. At the bottom of the jar the liquid will always be sufficiently thick.

title: Swiss Pudding (Swiss Pudding)
description: A pudding made with lemon extract, flour, and baking powder.

ingredients.name: 4 ounces or 6 large tablespoons granulated sugar

steps: Sift the flour together with baking powder and salt.
Rub the sugar and butter together well; when mixed but not creamy, gradually add the flour.
Make a hollow in the center of the dough and add an egg, lemon extract, and milk.
Mix to a soft dough, place in a form greased well with butter and sprinkled well with flour.
Boil for approximately 3 hours; test with a stiff straw pushed down into it; if nothing sticks to the straw, it is done.
Turn the pudding out of the form and serve with crème sauce.

title: Sylf ide-Omelet (Sylphide Omelet)
description: Prepared with rice flour, cream or milk, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: 1/4 pound finely cut candied citrus peel

steps: Mix 35 drams rice flour with 3 measures cream or sweet milk
Bake well together with 35 drams butter, 35 drams powdered sugar and 25 drams ground sweet almonds, heating the butter gently but not hot
Gradually stir into the mixture 12 egg yolks, first beaten white
Stir in 1/4 pound washed currants and 1/4 pound finely cut candied citrus peel
Finally fold in the 12 egg whites, first beaten to stiff peaks
As an alternative to the dried fruits, half a measure of liqueur can be added to the mixture
Bake the omelet and serve with sweet fruit sauce, liqueur can be added to taste according to preference
This amount makes 10-12 portions

title: Syltede Crabebler (Preserved Crabapples)
description: Prepared with juice, sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: 12 pounds sugar per pound of fruit
1 small cup water per pound of fruit
Juice of 1 lemon per 3 pounds of fruit

steps: Choose the best red crabapples. With the stems on, place them in the pot and pour warm water over them, enough to cover them.
Bring it to a boil and boil slowly until the skin cracks. Then cool, drain and peel them, then remove the cores from the top where the flower sits with a penknife.
Bring water and sugar to a boil for each pound of fruit (using 12 pounds sugar and 1 small cup water), and skim it well.
Then add the fruit and boil evenly under a lid until it is clear, soft and red.
Then take up the apples with a fish slice and spread them out on platters to cool and become firm.
To the syrup in the pot add the juice of 1 lemon for every 3 pounds of fruit and cook until it is smooth and clear.
Fill the fruit into crocks or glasses with enough room above to pour the syrup over, and when it is cold, tie them up.

Add some whole cloves and a piece of cinnamon to the boiling syrup.
If the stones are in the peaches, add them to the syrup and cook for 15 to 20 minutes; if the stones have been removed, place the peaches in jars and pour the hot syrup over them.
Place a small saucer or plate over them to keep them submerged in the syrup and tie them.
After four days, check them; if necessary, cook the syrup again and pour hot over them.
Store in a cool place while the weather is warm to prevent them from becoming sour.

Skim well, then add the kernels, sliced into thin slices.

Cook 1 pound white sugar to a thin syrup with 1 pint of the water in which the carrots were cooked
Add the carrots and juice of two lemons and cook about 10 minutes
Place in a crock and let stand two days

description: Prepared with apples, white sugar, and lemon juice.

steps: The apples must be good and juicy

Place 1 pound apples over the fire with 1 quart water and a couple of pieces of cinnamon
When it boils, add the apples, and when they have had 2 boilings, place them on a coarse strainer so the water can drain off
Boil 1 pound white sugar to syrup with ½ pint of the water in which the apples were cooked
Add these along with a little lemon juice, and boil very gently until they are clear, usually 5 minutes
Then remove the pot from the fire, let the apples stand a little in it, then remove them and place in a jar
If the juice is not stiff when cold, boil it a little more and pour cold over the apples

steps: Beat the white ginger for a while to check if it is dried; discard any dried pieces, but keep the good ones

title: Syltet Melon (Pickled Melon)
description: Prepared with melon, vinegar, and sugar.

ingredients.name: melon, fully grown but not ripe

steps: The melon must be fully grown but not ripe.
Peel it and cut it into 8 pieces.
Remove the interior.
Give the pieces a brief boil in water, remove and place on a clean linen cloth.
Meanwhile cook a sugar brine of 4 gills vinegar and 1 pound sugar.
Place the melon pieces in it to cook a little until the brine is as thick as syrup.

title: Tremont-Biscuits
description: A biscuit made with fat, white sugar, and cake or yeast.

ingredients.name: 1/2 cake compressed yeast or 1 cup homemade yeast

steps: Make a well in the center of 2 quarts sifted flour.
Add 1 3/8 pints warm milk, 1 tablespoon fat, 2 tablespoons white sugar, salt, and 1/2 cake compressed yeast or 1 cup homemade yeast, and blend together to form a dough.
Let it rise. When light, knead again and set to rise again.
When risen again, knead lightly and roll out 1 inch thick.

Dampen the corners slightly with melted butter and fold together with the point to the center.
Place on a bread pan with about 1 inch spacing.
Let them rise about half an hour in a warm place, then bake in a quick oven for 10 to 15 minutes.

If making for afternoon tea, set the dough in the morning. If for breakfast, set around 9 p.m., and as soon as you rise in the morning, add 1/2 teaspoon soda. They will then be ready for baking. They are considered very delicate when well made.

title: Valnødder (Pickled Walnuts)
description: Prepared with walnuts, icing sugar, and water.
steps: Pick walnuts in the first half of July before the stone has hardened
Pierce the meat and outer green shell with a coarse larding needle or bacon needle
Place in cold water, which must be renewed daily
After standing thus for about ten days, place over heat in cold water and cook covered until tender enough to pierce easily with a needle
Remove and place on a cloth, then weigh them
Boil sugar and water to a thin syrup and pour over the nuts, which stand thus for a couple of days
Drain off the juice, reduce well, and give the walnuts another boil in it
Place in glasses and reduce the juice further before pouring over

The walnuts can be flavored with various additions: either cook a stick of vanilla in the syrup, or stick the nuts with small pieces of cinnamon and some whole cloves after they have been cooked tender in the water. The spices mentioned can also be simply boiled in the syrup

title: Valnødder (Preserved Walnuts)
description: Prepared with walnuts, white sugar, and water.
steps: Walnuts are usually suitable for preserving in late July. They must only be half-grown and not yet have a hard shell, which can be tested by pricking with a larding needle; if there is nothing hard in them, they are good and are placed for 5 days in well water, which is renewed each day
Then prick them all around with a larding needle, and place them again in water for 4 days, which is likewise renewed each day
Then place them on the fire in cold water and cook under a lid until they are so tender that a pointed piece of cinnamon can be stuck through them, then place them on a cloth to drain and weigh them
Stick each walnut with 4 pieces of cinnamon and 2 cloves, and place in a crock
For each pound of nuts take 1 pound white sugar, which is cooked to a syrup with 3 gills water, and poured immediately over the walnuts, which then stand covered for 4 to 5 days

Then strain them, and the syrup is cooked with an addition of ½ pound sugar for 10 minutes, or until it is smooth, and is then poured immediately over the walnuts, which the next day are covered with paper dipped in brandy, and tied
If the syrup after about 3 weeks has become thin, it must be cooked again, but is then poured cold over the walnuts

title: Vandchokolade på Parisermaade (Parisian-style Water Chocolate)
description: A chocolate drink made with water and egg yolks, with optional sugar.
steps: Dissolve 4 Unzer fine chocolate in 1 Pint water
Pour into a high kettle and place on gentle heat and boil
After it has boiled for 10 minutes, whisk it with an egg whisk, which is twirled between the hands therein, until it froths strongly
Pour gradually into 2 beaten egg yolks, which have been beaten throughout the work
Return to the kettle and whisk continuously with the egg whisk
All the thin foam is placed with a skimmer in the heated cups, which are placed in a warm spot, and this is continued until it stands piled up in the form of a dome over the cups
Hold a red-hot fire shovel very close over the foam until a kind of crust forms, after which the chocolate is served

Note: The chocolate froths even better when some sugar is stirred into the egg yolks, or if foam balls are used instead, prepared as follows: A sufficient number of egg whites are whisked to very stiff foam, and therein is stirred fine powdered sugar until the mass forms a stiff dough, which is spread on a baking sheet, and when it is nearly dried, small balls are formed of the size of a medium nut, which are then dried completely in the sun or at room temperature. After the egg yolks are whipped together with the chocolate in the manner described above, for each cup one such foam ball is placed in the chocolate pot and whisked on the fire until the entire chocolate mass is dissolved into stiff foam. One must observe the precaution that the chocolate is only heated until nearly boiling; it must absolutely not boil.

title: Vildsvinehoved (Wild Boar Head)
description: Prepared with red wine, stock, and onions.
steps: Cut off the head at the shoulder blades as the neck is the greatest delicacy.

Remove the eyes and clean the head very thoroughly and wrap it in thin cloth.
Boil for at least 3 hours in a marinade of red wine and stock with 2 chopped onions, 1 celery, 2 carrots, 2 bay leaves, 1 lemon sliced, some whole peppercorns and a little juniper berries.
When cooked, set aside and only when cold, remove from the soup, unwrap, and garnish for serving.
Cut the neck meat into slices, reassemble them, and arrange the head on a platter garnished with green salad.
Place a whole lemon in the snout and replace the eyes with 2 slices of hard-boiled eggs with a black peppercorn in each.

Mix fat and butter with lemon juice and pipe through a piping bag to create decorative figures on the head, which can also be covered with stiff stock and cut vegetables or simply wrapped with flowers stuck into the head.

Serve Cumberland Sauce on the side: reduce some of the soup in which the head was cooked until it becomes a strong stock, add the juice of 1 or 2 lemons along with the peel of 1 orange with the white skin well removed, bring to a boil, and stir in red wine, mustard and paprika to taste, strain and thicken with dissolved tapioca flour.

title: Vindruer (Preserved Grapes)

title: Yankee Pork and Beans
description: Prepared with white beans, lard, and molasses or syrup.
steps: Soak one quart of small white beans in cold water overnight.
The next morning, strain them into fresh water and let them dry.
Place them in cold water with 3 tablespoons of soda over the fire; let them boil for approximately half an hour and drain the water.
Take an earthenware pot and place a slice of lard in the bottom, then the beans with two or three tablespoons of molasses.
Next place in the center 1 to 3 pounds of salt pork with the skin scored crosswise; add a little pepper and, if needed, a little salt.
Pour boiling water over until it covers the meat.
Let it bake 6 hours or more over an even, moderate fire, adding boiling water as needed to keep it moist as evaporation requires.
It cannot easily be baked too long.
Keep the lid on to prevent scorching on top, but remove it for one hour before serving so the pork becomes crispy.

Remove the pot from the fire and shake the berries well, then let them rest until they appear clear and full, then divide into smaller jars and treat in the usual manner.
If desired, the stones can be crushed, the kernels removed and mixed with the berries.

title: Ægte Skildpaddesuppe (Genuine Turtle Soup)
description: A soup made with turtle, beef, and ham.

ingredients.name: 40 pounds beef and veal shank (for 60-pound turtle)

steps: Place the turtle on a straw-covered board and pull out the neck with a rope as far as possible, then cut off the head
If the turtle is large, allow 10 to 12 hours for the blood to drain
Open it with a knife inserted between the belly and back shell
Cut off the flippers, neck and tail as close to the body as possible
Remove the intestines first, then the meat and bones, and finally the fat attached to the shell
Cut the belly and back shells into large squares and cook for a few minutes until the fine outer shell can be removed
Treat the flippers, tail and head the same way; cook everything in water until the meat can be loosened from the bones, which are set aside for serving
Scald the greenish fat with water and cook it for 3 quarters of an hour with wine and bouillon; the reddish meat is cooked tender in the bouillon but is not served

Brown approximately 40 pounds of beef and veal shank in butter or good fat in a large pot together with 8 onions, 2 carrots, 2 celeries, 2 leeks, a little thyme, 3 bay leaves, some peppercorns and cloves
Pour it up with the bouillon in which the turtle was cooked, with the addition of salt
After 5 hours of cooking, remove the meat and strain the soup through a fine sieve
A few hours before serving, pour about 4 quarts of turtle bouillon (calculated for 12 persons) into a casserole
Add a hen browned together with the giblets, 3 pounds lean veal in square pieces, ¼ pound ham, cut vegetables, seasonings and parsley
Bring to a boil, move to a gentler heat, add ½ pint Madeira and continue cooking for 1 hour; the soup should then be clear and pale yellow in color
Skim and strain through a sieve into another casserole
Mix it with the necessary amount of turtle meat and the flippers cut into cubes
When it has cooked with these for 12 to 15 minutes, add a little cayenne, a glass of seasoning extract and some of the turtle fat cut into cubes
Pour the soup into the tureen and serve with lemon slices
